conditions: if the US bans Chinese models

statement.excerpt: Variant on the above; sure to raise prices to consumers, and stifle innovation.
statement.document_title: China has all but caught up. The US is not going to “win” the AI war. Here’s what we should do instead.

from_speaker: sure to raise prices to consumers
our_interpretation: Altogether means an implemented general US prohibition on Chinese AI models, including ordinary commercial and consumer use. A restriction on federal agencies or one vendor alone does not establish that condition.
Consumer prices means prices paid by US end users for comparable AI services.
Stifle innovation means a material reduction in new products, model improvements, or market entry caused by the ban.
Both effects are evaluated against what would have happened without the ban.
criteria.support_condition: A qualifying general ban takes effect and credible causal evidence establishes both higher consumer prices and reduced innovation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete evaluation of a qualifying ban establishes that consumer prices did not rise because of it or that innovation was not suppressed. Brief post-ban observations alone are insufficient.
